Performing initial audit of PKGBUILD to ensure that we can safely run `makepkg`
LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>UNSAFE</decision>
<details>
**Scope:** `makepkg --printsrcinfo` sources the PKGBUILD , executing only its global/top-level statements. Functions (`pkgver`, `build`, `package`) are defined but not invoked.  
**Risk:** The file uses HTML entities (`&quot;` and `&apos;`) in place of standard shell quotes (`"` and `'`). When the shell sources this file, it does **not** decode these entities. It treats every bare `&` as a control operator (which backgrounds the preceding simple command or breaks the current token list) and parses the surrounding text as **new commands to be executed**.  For example:  
- `pkgdesc=&quot;Find the real capacity …` becomes an empty assignment to `pkgdesc`, then attempts to run `Find`, `the`, `real`, `capacity`, etc. as commands.  
- `url=&quot;https://github.com/…` tries to execute the entire URL `https://github.com/9M2PJU/Adromedarys-s-True-Flasher.` as a command.  
- `depends=(&apos;gcc-libs&apos; …)` backgrounds the broken array assignment and runs `apos`, `gcc-libs`, … as commands.  

This is a classic shell injection at source‑time. Running `makepkg --printsrcinfo` would execute arbitrary text from the PKGBUILD as commands, which is dangerous.
</details>
<evidence>
pkgdesc="Find the real capacity of fake USB flash drives"
url="https://github.com/9M2PJU/Adromedarys-s-True-Flasher."
depends=('gcc-libs' 'util-linux')
source=("git+https://github.com/9M2PJU/Adromedarys-s-True-Flasher..git")
</evidence>
<summary>
Shell injection via HTML entity quoting.
</summary>
</security_assessment>

Second look for PKGBUILD (incontext):
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The original verdict incorrectly interpreted the `"` and `'` sequences as literal file content rather than as XML encoding artifacts introduced by the way the file was presented. In the actual PKGBUILD, these would be ordinary double and single quotes (`"` and `'`). With the correct quoting, the global scope contains only standard variable assignments, a source array pointing to the project's own GitHub repository, and function definitions. No global‑scope command substitution, download, or exfiltration occurs. Therefore, running `makepkg --printsrcinfo` on this PKGBUILD is safe.
</details>
<evidence></evidence>
<summary>HTML entities are artifacts; file is safe.</summary>
</security_assessment>

+ Initial PKGBUILD audit complete -- HTML entities are artifacts; file is safe.
